milestone.title: Testing quality: gap tests, hermetic rules, coverage floor re-baseline

intent.outcome: StowEngine missing-binary and dry-run behaviors are unit-tested without requiring a happy-path stow install for those cases; doctor script behavior without stow on PATH is asserted; --help smoke test exists; AGENTS documents the testing cheat sheet; coverage floors are re-measured and raised only if safe. Depends on testing infrastructure milestone so nextest/coverage tooling is in place.

problem.description: After M01–M07, known test gaps remain: StowEngine has almost no unit coverage (relies on stow e2e fixtures); doctor optional-stow messaging is untested; CLI --help has no binary smoke test; AGENTS lacks a short which-target-when testing cheat sheet; coverage floors may be stale after native engine landed. Without explicit gap tests and docs, regressions slip past green suites (L1).

in_scope: andre-core unit tests: StowEngine missing-binary (PATH isolation) and dry_run no FS writes
Doctor: check_dependencies.sh exit 0 without stow on PATH (optional messaging OK); wire into make test/ci or dedicated target
AGENTS.md Testing cheat sheet aligned with M08 targets
make coverage-check; raise floors only with headroom; else record measured % in evidence
Optional: nextest filterset or make target for stow-required e2e only
out_of_scope: Product features (engine parity, adopt via LinkEngine, regex ignore)

design_decisions.choice: Prefer a small shell or Rust test that runs check_dependencies.sh with PATH stripped of stow; do not require interactive TTY colors
design_decisions.rationale: Matches AC-03 spirit from M07 without flaking on color codes
Test-only + docs; PATH isolation needs care under nextest parallelism

findings.description: andre/tests/smoke.rs header comment for doctor_exits_zero_when_stow_missing claims 'cargo test and nextest both serialize test functions that touch env' — this is FALSE. cargo test runs multiple test functions within a single binary in parallel threads (default test-threads = num-cpus). nextest 0.9+ runs each test in its own process (true serialization at the binary level, but multiple processes run in parallel). Empirically verified: in a 3-test binary where path_manipulator sleeps 500ms after setting PATH, the other two slow tests see the modified PATH in their env::var() output. The current smoke binary has only one env-mutating test so the race does not manifest, but the comment will mislead future developers who add a second PATH-touching test. Fix: replace the false claim with the truthful invariant: 'This test mutates PATH in the test binary's process. The andre::smoke binary currently has no other test that reads PATH, so no race in practice. Any future smoke test that reads PATH (e.g., a  check) MUST wrap its env::var() in the catch_unwind+set_var dance.' Also: andre-core/src/engine.rs has the analogous wrong comment ('nextest + cargo test both isolate binaries' — true at the binary level, but the implication that 'subsequent tests in this binary' won't observe the override is wrong under cargo test's intra-binary parallelism).

.woodpecker/base.yml test step installs cargo-llvm-cov but make ci (the only thing the test step runs) does not use llvm-cov — only the coverage step uses llvm-cov. The redundant install adds ~30-60s to CI runtime (cargo install cargo-llvm-cov pulls llvm-tools-preview if missing). Fix: remove the cargo install cargo-llvm-cov line from the test step's commands. Keep it in the coverage step. The header comment line 4 ('install python3 (used by scripts/coverage-check.py)') is also misleading because the test step doesn't install python3 — only the coverage step does. Either move that comment down to the coverage step description or remove it.

scripts/coverage-summary.sh and scripts/test-count.sh are now orphaned dead code. Both were introduced by M42-WP0 (commit e5e88b7) to support the awk-based 'cargo llvm-cov --summary-only' coverage-check target. M08 replaced that target with scripts/coverage-check.py (consuming 'cargo llvm-cov report --json'), and the Makefile no longer references the old scripts (verified: grep -r 'coverage-summary\|test-count' Makefile scripts/ andre/ andre-core/ AGENTS.md returns nothing). They are still executable and tracked in git but unused. Fix: delete both files. They can always be recovered from git history if needed.
